messages:
anya: Heads up — starting a small project to rebuild the 'privileged-runner' base image into a PCI-scoped variant. Need to lock down RBAC for the image-builder SA, wire audit logs to secure-syslog, and coordinate KMS signer access. Target: complete canary by tomorrow morning.

devon: +1. what's the plan for KMS keys? we should avoid giving long-lived key access to the runner process.

anya: plan is to use short-lived keywrap via kms-operator with 1h leases. image-builder SA will get token-scoped credential via OIDC provider from our build cluster.

marco: will that require clusterrole changes? currently kms-operator needs clusterrole-binding to the build namespace for wrapping.

anya: yes — minimal change: add a RoleBinding in infra-builds namespace granting kms-operator/wrap to image-builder serviceaccount. no cluster-admin.

sam: can you drop the kubectl snippet here so infra can review? also want audit log route config.

anya: sure — snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: kms-wrap-for-image-builder
  namespace: infra-builds
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: kms-wrap-role
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: image-builder
    namespace: infra-builds
```

anya: For audit logs: builder nodes will POST structured events to /ingest/prod/pci with a signed token. If Splunk is down, fallback pushes to encrypted S3 bucket (audit-archive/pci).

devon: sounds reasonable. who owns the ingestion endpoint cert/key rotation?

sam: ops owns endpoint TLS, secops owns the Splunk routing. auditor-bot: NOTE: ensure audit events include container image digest, cosign signature ID, and KMS wrap key id. These fields are required for PCI evidence.

marco: quick vuln-triage note — image contains libnss 3.72 (CVE-2025-xxxx). patch available in upstream base. we'll rebuild with patched packages.

anya: added to the canary checklist. also enabling seccomp profile and read-only rootfs in the image runtime config.

devon: will applying seccomp/read-only break any of the image-builder hooks? we have a preflight script that writes to /tmp.

sam: change preflight to use /run/tmp and mark that mount as tmpfs in the pod spec. should be fine.

marco: small nit — cosign signer key access: prefer HSM-bound short-lived signing tokens. ops can grant cosign-sa permission to call kms-operator/sign only for the signing slot.

anya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/824 — adds RoleBinding, audit route, and canary job. Please review by EOD.

devon: reviewing now. tagging infra: @sam @marco :thumbsup:

sam: reviewed and left one comment about S3 lifecycle.

auditor-bot: REMINDER: Once canary completes, upload evidence bundle to secure-artifacts and poke the compliance ticket.

anya: noted. I'll run the canary tonight at 22:00 UTC and post results here.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist: canary job scheduled — job id cj-2026-0912-01 — monitoring on #release-war-room.

devon: thanks — if anything blocks the keywrap flow I'll escalate.

anya: thanks all — will post results. :rocket:
